items.title: Eddie Palmieri — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bernard Purdie. I mean, it is serious business now, the heavy-heavy-heavy.

ctx.x: But this is a significant album. Like you mentioned, you were doing crossover. So now you’re not just blending Caribbean music...

In my opinion, it’s one of the finest albums ever recorded. My opinion of where it went. Ronnie Cuber. He worked with the Aretha Franklin band. You’ve got Cornell Dupree, who passed away. Bernard Purdie. I mean, it is serious business now, the heavy-heavy-heavy. Then Randy Brecker with Burt Collins, trumpet. Ronnie Cuber brought him in on baritone—who is known as the God of the Baritone. A gentleman called Jimmy Norman, who sang with the Commodores, and he just passed away. It seems like... I’m going to be very…
